claims.value: Toreno gives side A 34,000 facing the Spaniards, excluding Victor’s 14,000 on the flank; the larger combined possibility is not a force all engaged.
claims.rationale: Opponent estimate; Jourdan says immediate attack precluded Victor’s arrival. Not summed into battlefield strength. English rendering (ours): "He faced thirty-four thousand in front, not counting Victor’s fourteen thousand on his right flank."

claims.value: Jourdan gives Mortier the two corps’ infantry, Sebastiani the cavalry, and Joseph with his major-general overall movements.
claims.rationale: Soult is the major-general in the preceding narrative. Separate scopes, not equal or automatic credit. English rendering (ours): "Mortier commanded the two corps’ infantry, Sebastiani the cavalry; the king and his major-general directed the movements."

claims.value: Toreno places Areizaga observing from a bell tower, Zayas on the opposite wing and Lacy further right.
claims.rationale: The same paragraph assigns Zayas and Lacy sectors. Toreno’s hostile judgment of Areizaga is attributed, not proof of inability. English rendering (ours): "He climbed a town bell tower, from which he contented himself with observing the field."

claims.value: Jourdan describes the French decision to attack without waiting for Victor.
claims.rationale: The preceding sentences explain waiting for Victor was rejected; Spanish local counterattack across the ravine is not a second main offensive. English rendering (ours): "They decided to attack."
